name: Bhutan
headline: Bhutan: +8.2% growth in 2025, 2.6% inflation, debt 103% of GDP
sections: Bhutan is a $3.5 billion economy (2025), the world's 182nd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +8.2% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $20K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 6.6% of GDP (2024).

Consumer prices rose 2.6% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 5.9% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.2% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 17.1% (2025).
Gross government debt is 103% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has fallen from 116% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.7% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −16.0% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 79% of GDP (2024), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.2% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 116% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 73.3 years (2024). Population: 791 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
